Start a vulnerability scan of a package version

Start a vulnerability scan of one version of a package. The server answers 202
and scans in the background; its Location header names the scan, which rp
prints. A manual scan runs whatever the repository's automatic scan setting
says, but not when scanning is switched off on the server (code scannerDisabled).

With a scanner enabled every upload starts a scan on its own, so a trigger right
after 'rp push' meets a scan that is already running (HTTP 409, code
scanAlreadyRunning). rp then attaches to that scan instead of failing: with
--wait it waits for it and applies --fail-on; without --wait it prints the
running scan's id and status and exits 0 (a note on stderr says it attached).

--scope is the npm scope without the "@" (scoped npm packages only).

In a Maven repository the artifact is groupId:artifactId (for example
com.acme:app); the server finds nothing for the bare artifactId, so rp refuses
it. The other formats take the plain package name.

--wait polls until the scan is COMPLETED or FAILED (the server has no status
endpoint): first every --poll-interval, then slower, up to 15 seconds. It gives
up after --timeout (default 10m) with a timeout error, which is NOT the
threshold error: it exits 1, says nothing about the findings, and the scan
keeps running on the server.

--fail-on critical|high|medium|low exits 5 when the scan has a finding at or
above that severity; UNKNOWN findings never count. A scan that FAILED, or that
is not final yet, cannot be judged: that is an error with exit 1, not a pass.
Exit codes: 0 passed, 5 threshold reached, 1 timeout or other failure.

Examples:
```
rp scan trigger libs my-app 1.2.0
rp scan trigger maven-libs com.acme:my-app 1.2.0 --wait --fail-on high
```

```
rp scan trigger <repo> <artifact> <version> [flags]
```

## Options

```
      --fail-on string           Exit 5 when a finding has this severity or worse (critical, high, medium, low)
      --poll-interval duration   First pause between polls; it grows up to 15s (with --wait) (default 2s)
      --scope string             npm scope, without the @
      --timeout duration         Give up waiting after this long (with --wait) (default 10m0s)
      --wait                     Wait until the scan is COMPLETED or FAILED
```
